Although AirPods equipped with cameras are not expected to launch until next year, a Bloomberg report indicates that Apple may unveil the AirPods 5 as early as next month's anticipated iPhone event. Here are the details.

AirPods 5 will be available in both a standard version and an Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) version

In a wide-ranging report published earlier tonight, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said Apple may unveil a new-generation Mac mini in the coming days, earlier than the expected September event.

Gurman also detailed several other products Apple has in the pipeline, including the AirPods 5, which could make its debut as early as next month. He noted that the company is expected to hold its next event on 9 September, at which it will simultaneously launch its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro series, and new Apple Watch models.

The report reads as follows:

The company is also preparing a series of minor updates to the Apple Watch, including upgrades to fitness-tracking features and a new ceramic case option for the Series 12 model. In addition, Apple plans to launch the next generation of AirPods as early as its September product event. According to sources, the lineup will include the all-new AirPods 5, serving as an update to Apple's entry-level earbuds. The model was last updated back in 2024. As for the camera-equipped version of the AirPods, it is not expected to arrive until next year.

Interestingly, after publishing his report, Gurman posted a follow-up on X, adding that the AirPods 5 is expected to launch simultaneously in both a standard version and a noise-cancelling version:

Although there has been little reporting on the launch timing of the AirPods 5, the general expectation is that the earbuds will not arrive until 2027. In addition, Apple is reportedly developing two models of camera-equipped AirPods, which will offer AI-powered features through Visual Intelligence and Siri.

Apple recently accidentally included a demo video of the camera-equipped AirPods in the macOS 26.7 candidate release, although the clip did not clearly show what differences the device has in appearance.
